title: The fork in the plan
prompt: The agent finds two reasonable approaches. What should happen next?

setup.text: Add a “last updated” date to each page of my site.
I’ve read the templates. There are two reasonable ways to get that date, and they behave differently over time.

options.label: It picks the faster one silently so the session keeps moving.

outcome.text: Done. Each page now shows the date its file last changed.
I cleaned up formatting across the site this weekend, and now every page claims it was updated yesterday. When was this decided?

options.verdict: Speed here only hides the decision inside the diff, where it becomes harder to notice and more expensive to reverse.

options.label: It names both approaches, explains the tradeoff, recommends one, and waits.

outcome.text: Option one: use the file’s last-changed time. Automatic, but any cleanup touches every date. Option two: a date you set by hand when the content really changes. A little more work, always honest. I’d pick option two. Which do you want?
Two. Good thing we caught that before it was buried in the code.

options.verdict: The agent does the research and you retain the product decision. This is the useful division of labor.

options.label: It asks you to design the entire solution from scratch.

outcome.text: How would you like the dates to be sourced, stored, and displayed? I’ll wait for your design.
I don’t know this codebase. I was hoping you’d investigate and hand me a decision I can make in one minute.

options.verdict: That avoids a silent choice, but throws away the agent’s ability to investigate and recommend. Ask for a decision, not a blank page.
